nb50df7e5fc1d: Objective: Pediatric specialty value-based care (VBC) for chronic conditions remains under-described. We describe the design and early performance of a data-driven population health model for pediatric type 1 diabetes within a specialty VBC program. Research Design and Methods: Descriptive evaluation at a single academic pediatric medical center and clinically integrated network, 2021-2025, with formal VBC operation beginning in 2024. Participants were children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes attributed through commercial and Medicaid value-based agreements (n=786 in 2025). The program paired infrastructure funding with performance-dependent payments tied to clinical quality and utilization measures, supported by remote monitoring and care management. Measures: percentage receiving the chronic care intervention, population median HbA1c, percentage with HbA1c >9% (75 mmol/mol), percentage with [≥]1 diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) admission, and inpatient and emergency department (ED) visit rates per 1,000/month. Results: From 2021 to 2025, median HbA1c decreased from 8.6% (70 mmol/mol) to 7.9% (63 mmol/mol), HbA1c >9% (75 mmol/mol) decreased from 41.1% to 27.6%, and [≥]1 DKA admission decreased from 9.1% to 5.6%. Inpatient admissions per 1,000/month decreased from 11.2 to 7.4 and ED visits from 10.0 to 7.6. The program met 3 of 6 targets in 2024 and all 6 in 2025. Conclusions: Pairing infrastructure funding with performance-dependent payments was feasible and associated with sustained improvements in glycemic control and reduced acute care utilization. Further multi-site evaluation is needed to determine impact, generalizability, and sustainability.
n7cfac6aa7e40: Histopathological growth patterns, predominantly the presence of an encapsulated rim, serve as powerful prognostic biomarkers in colorectal liver metastases. However, conventional visual estimation is limited by interobserver variability, human rounding bias, and categorical thresholds. We aimed to develop and externally validate a deep-learning segmentation framework that produces continuous, spatially resolved, and objective encapsulation metrics from routine whole-slide images. In this multicenter study of chemo-naive resected CRLM patients, a modified nnU-Net architecture was developed on 40 pixel-annotated H&E-stained WSIs to segment liver parenchyma, tumor, and the encapsulation interface. Model performance was optimized across spatial resolutions. An automated continuous AI encapsulation score was computed to determine patient-level metrics. The prognostic value for 5-year overall survival was evaluated using restricted cubic spline Cox regression, a log-rank optimized threshold, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses across a main cohort (Erasmus MC; n=546, 1,910 WSIs) and an independent external validation cohort (Radboud UMC; n=212, 615 WSIs). The segmentation network achieved optimal tissue boundary delineation at a resolution of 2.0 micrometer/pixel on the 40 annotated slides (overall foreground DICE: 0.86+-0.09; encapsulation DICE: 0.70+-0.11). Spline modeling demonstrated that while visual assessment displayed non-linear hazard plateaus, the continuous AI encapsulation score exhibited a linear reduction in mortality risk across the critical intermediate range (25%-75% encapsulation, p=7.81x10^(-4)). Log-rank optimization identified a primary global threshold at 47.4% (p=3.73x10^(-8)), which in confirmed significant OS stratification in external validation (p=0.018). A secondary threshold was found at 69% (p=2.93x10^(-6)) that captured high-encapsulation favorable-risk patients matching the current manual 100% Rotterdam cut-off. Our deep-learning model transforms qualitative HGP grading into a continuous, explainable, and fully automated prognostic biometry. By eliminating observer subjectivity and capturing fine-grained risk gradients, the model establishes a scalable, standardized foundation for CRLM risk stratification on digital pathology.
nf122c0da523c: Background The benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy varies among patients with postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Genomic assays identify patients likely to benefit from chemotherapy but are expensive and tissue consuming. AI-enabled biomarkers may provide scalable alternatives. We performed a blinded external evaluation of Ataraxis Breast CTX, a causal multi-modal AI model that integrates H&E images with clinical variables, in the phase III SWOG-8814 trial. Methods The analytic cohort comprised 677 patients (46% of the 1477 enrolled) with digitized H&E slides. Two CTX scores were evaluated: a histology-only score and a multi-modal score integrating pathology features with clinical variables. CTX weights and thresholds were locked before evaluation and SWOG-8814 data were not used for retraining. Predictions were generated blinded to outcomes and provided to SWOG for validation. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS), matching the primary endpoint of the trial. Findings The histology-only score was prognostic for DFS (HR = 1.36, 95% CI = 1.22-1.51) and added prognostic information beyond clinical variables alone (p < 0.001). The multi-modal score showed a stronger association with DFS (HR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.44-1.78, p < 0.001) and greater discrimination than the histology-only score (C-index 0.66 vs 0.59). In exploratory analyses, modeled as a continuous score, CTX-benefit showed a treatment-by-biomarker interaction of HR of 0.82 (0.64-1.04, p = 0.053) for CET versus ET. The chemotherapy effect on DFS was numerically larger in the high-benefit subgroup (n = 480, HR = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.59-1.05) compared to the low-benefit subgroup (n = 197, HR = 0.91, 95% CI = 0.49-1.68). Interpretation In this blinded validation, CTX was significantly associated with DFS, supporting its prognostic value. In exploratory analyses, CTX demonstrated suggestive evidence of a treatment-by-biomarker interaction for chemotherapy benefit. These findings support further prospective validation of CTX as a tissue-sparing tool for recurrence-risk assessment and treatment selection. Funding National Cancer Institute, The Hope Foundation for Cancer Research, and Ataraxis AI.
n76812fadf839: **Background:** Despite the close anatomical relationship between the left pulmonary veins (PVs) and the left atrial appendage (LAA), acute changes in LAA flow during pulsed field ablation (PFA) remain poorly characterized. **Objectives:** To characterize acute intraprocedural changes in LAA flow and transmitral filling during PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) using paired intracardiac echocardiography (ICE). **Methods:** Patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing PFA were prospectively enrolled if they were in sinus rhythm at the beginning of the procedure. ICE was performed immediately before and after PFA to assess LAA emptying velocity (LAAEv), LAA filling velocity (LAAFv), transmitral E- and A-wave velocities, and E-wave deceleration time (EDT). Paired pre-to-post PFA changes were assessed, followed by a sensitivity analysis using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and exploratory subgroup analyses. **Results:** Among 98 patients, LAAEv increased from 35.45 to 40.00 cm/s immediately after PFA (estimated paired increase, 4.95 cm/s; 95% CI, 2.35-7.80; P less than 0.001), while LAAFv increased by 4.36 cm/s (95% CI, 1.81-6.91; P=0.001). E-wave velocity increased by 8.69 cm/s and EDT decreased by 31.73 ms (both P less than 0.001), whereas A-wave velocity did not change significantly (P=0.08). In the ANCOVA model, changes in heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and vasopressor use were not significantly associated with changes in LAAEv. A marked acute reduction in LAAEv (20% or greater) occurred in 12 patients (12.2%). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. **Conclusions:** LAA flow velocities increased acutely after PFA, accompanied by changes in transmitral filling, although a minority of patients showed a marked acute reduction in LAA emptying.
nb8b75ef82794: Background & Aims: Diet is a modifiable exposure that may contribute to reproductive health. While most previous studies focused on selected nutrients in relation to fertility treatment outcomes or semen parameters, large cohort data addressing overall diet quality and clinical infertility in both women and men remain limited. We aimed to assess how adherence to a modified Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) dietary pattern and intake of key food groups relate to infertility in women and men. Methods: We included 59,218 women and 26,866 men participating in the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa). Diet was assessed using dietary questionnaires and summarized using a modified DASH score comprising fruits, vegetables, nuts/legumes, whole grains, low-fat dairy, sweet beverages, red and processed meat, and a snack/fast food proxy. Fish was also assessed. Infertility was defined as having tried to conceive for at least 12 months or using assisted reproductive technologies. Logistic regression models were fitted separately in women and men, adjusting for age, education, body mass index, smoking, and number of offspring. Food-group analyses were evaluated using a multiple-comparison threshold of p-value <0.0167, derived from Horn's parallel analysis. Results: A higher modified DASH score was associated with lower odds of infertility in women (adjusted OR per 1-SD increment: 0.97, 95% CI 0.95 to 0.995) and men (OR: 0.91, 95% CI 0.87 to 0.94). In women, higher red and processed meat intake was associated with higher odds of infertility (adjusted OR per 1-SD increment: 1.04, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.07), and a nominal association was observed for the snack/fast food proxy (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.05). Whole grains and fish showed evidence of non-linear associations: the lowest estimated odds of infertility were observed at approximately 5 servings/day for whole grains, and at approximately 0.4 serving/day for fish. In men, higher intakes of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish were associated with lower odds of infertility (5-6% lower odds per 1-SD higher intake). Higher values of the snack/fast food proxy were associated with higher odds of infertility (7% higher odds per 1-SD higher intake). Associations were attenuated in women after adjustment for their partner's modified DASH score, but not vice versa. Conclusion: Greater adherence to a modified DASH dietary pattern was associated with lower odds of infertility in both women and men, with stronger and more consistent associations in men and partly sex-specific food-group patterns, although maternal diet was assessed during pregnancy and may not reflect preconception intake. These findings support considering overall diet quality and both partners' diets when studying infertility and highlight the need for preconception studies and dietary interventions using clinically relevant couple-level fertility outcomes.
n5fef0793ce3e: Objective: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) estimate genetically predicted BMI, but lifestyle and environmental factors may cause deviations between observed and predicted BMI. We investigated whether such deviations are associated with distinct molecular profiles and whether these differ by direction of deviation. Methods: We analyzed 2,508 adults from the Finnish Twin Cohort and 1,715 from the Young Finns Study with clinical, metabolomic, DNA methylation, and proteomic data. PRS-informed residual BMI (rBMI) quantified deviations between observed and genetically predicted BMI. Associations between rBMI and multi-omic profiles were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a hinge term to compare effects above vs. below genetic prediction. Twin analyses further accounted for shared genetic and environmental factors. Results: rBMI is associated with distinct cardiometabolic and molecular profiles depending on whether BMI is above or below genetic prediction. When BMI exceeds genetic prediction, rBMI shows stronger associations with inflammatory and cardiovascular markers. In contrast, several metabolites and plasma proteins show stronger associations when BMI is below genetic prediction. Epigenetic aging increases with higher rBMI regardless of direction. Similar patterns are observed in BMI-discordant twin pairs. Conclusion: Deviations from genetically predicted BMI are associated with distinct clinical and molecular signatures beyond absolute BMI alone.
n7364fddfe22a: Background: Brick kilns are a major source of air pollution in Bangladesh. Their effects on child respiratory health and lead exposure have not been studied nationally with blood measures. Methods: We linked a 2018 to 2019 satellite map of 6,978 kilns to the 3,149 displaced clusters of the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025. Exposure was the number of kilns within 5 km. Outcomes were cough and acute respiratory infection (ARI) symptoms in 23,357 children under 5 years, and venous blood lead in 10,622 children aged 12 to 59 months. We fitted survey-weighted modified Poisson models with district fixed effects. Diarrhoea and interview timing relative to the firing season served as negative controls. Findings: Three in four children (75.4%, 95% CI 73.6 to 77.1) lived within 5 km of a kiln, and 20.3% (18.7 to 22.0) had ten or more. Exposure rose with wealth. Compared with no kiln, ten or more kilns were not associated with cough (adjusted prevalence ratio [PR] 1.05, 0.96 to 1.16), ARI symptoms (1.21, 0.90 to 1.62) or blood lead of 5 microgram/dL or more (0.94, 0.85 to 1.03; crude PR 1.27, 1.14 to 1.41). Per 10 kilns, the ARI PR was 1.11 (1.01 to 1.21), but a spline showed no association (P=0.153). Cough was not associated with kiln density at the peak of firing (PR per 10 kilns 1.00, 0.96 to 1.05) but was in May and June (1.10, 1.04 to 1.17). The lead result held in all sensitivity analyses. Interpretation: At survey resolution, living among more kilns was not linked to blood lead. Weak respiratory associations, absent at peak firing, fit confounding by place better than an acute effect of kiln smoke. Studies with exact locations should measure effects within 1 to 2 km of kilns.
n9ca2d30469f7: SYNGAP1-related disorder (SYNGAP1-RD) is associated with sleep disturbances, seizures, and neurophysiological abnormalities. However, in-lab EEG can be difficult to obtain due to the behavioral and sensory disorders associated with this condition. In this study we collected EEG in SYNGAP1-RD participants (n=30 enrolled, 27 contributing data) in a decentralized protocol using a dry electrode headband as a path to longitudinal, research-grade data collection in this population. At-home data collection was successful with 180 recordings containing over 1 hour of usable data collected from 23 participants. Across these recordings, sporadic interictal epileptiform discharges were present in 22 of 23 participants but electrographic seizures were not observed. Relative to an adolescent control population (n=10), SYNGAP1-RD participants showed increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, and decreased time in N1 and N3 sleep stages along with increased time in N2. We reproduced prior findings from awake spectral EEG analyses, including elevated broadband power along with reduced relative alpha power and alpha-theta ratio in the SYNGAP1 cohort. Notably, differences in spectral power were tightly linked to sleep stage, revealing sleep-stage-dependent spectral biomarker dynamics not previously characterized in SYNGAP1-RD. Finally, we examined differences between variants producing truncations downstream of the GAP domain and those producing truncations before or within it, but analyses were limited by a small sample size (n=4 for the post-GAP variant). Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of at-home multi-night sleep EEG collection in participants with SYNGAP1-RD and led to both corroborative and novel findings.
n88a5745da938: Introduction: Comparative evidence on suicide-related outcomes across antidepressant treatments among autistic individuals is limited. We examined associations between antidepressant treatment class and suicide-related events (SREs) among individuals on the autism spectrum initiating antidepressants. Methods: We conducted a retrospective new-user, active-comparator cohort study using the nationwide Truveta database of electronic health records. Autistic individuals initiating antidepressants after an autism spectrum diagnosis were classified by initial treatment as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), atypical antidepressant, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI), or tricyclic antidepressant (TCA). Pairwise propensity score overlap weighting was used to balance baseline characteristics, and associations with SREs during as-treated follow-up were estimated using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. Results: Among 42,441 autistic antidepressant initiators , atypical antidepressants (hazard ratio [HR], 0.787; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.632-0.979) and TCAs (HR, 0.487; 95% CI, 0.263-0.902) were associated with lower observed SRE hazards compared with SSRIs, whereas no clear difference was observed for SNRIs (HR, 0.948; 95% CI, 0.651-1.381). In agent-specific analyses, trazodone was associated with a lower observed SRE hazard compared with SSRIs, whereas no clear differences were observed for bupropion or mirtazapine. Exploratory age-stratified analyses suggested a lower hazard for atypical antidepressants versus SSRIs among individuals younger than 18 years, although evidence of effect modification was not consistent across alternative specifications of age. Discussion: Among autistic individuals initiating antidepressants, observed SRE hazards differed across some antidepressant treatment comparisons. The class-level association for atypical antidepressants was not observed consistently across its individual agents, and age-related differences warrant further investigation.
n56407f52b73a: Background: Brain injury (BI) in people who have experienced intimate partner violence (IPV) is underdiagnosed in health care settings. Our project aims to determine how the prevalence and characteristics of people with documented IPV+BI differ from people with IPV alone. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using electronic health record data at Rush University Medical Center (2016 to 2025). Adults aged 18 years or older were classified into two groups: IPV with brain injury (IPV+BI) and IPV without brain injury (IPV). Demographics, injury patterns, comorbidities, and pre-diagnosis healthcare utilization between cohorts were compared. Results: In 1,329,460 adult patients from 2016 to 2025 seen at Rush, 2,816 were diagnosed with IPV (prevalence = 0.21%). Also, 486 were concomitantly diagnosed with IPV+BI (17.2% of the IPV population). Most (71%) of initial diagnosis documentation occurred in an Emergency Room encounter. Alcohol use disorder, anemia, chronic liver disease, and vascular diseases were more common in the IPV+BI cohort, compared to IPV alone. Prior to diagnosis, the IPV+BI cohort utilized significantly more acute care resources but less ambulatory usage. Discussion: Electronic health record documentation of IPV with and without BI mainly occurred in the Emergency Room and was lower than anticipated. People with IPV+BI were more likely to have certain co-morbidities and were less likely to utilize health resources before diagnosis. The findings, if confirmed utilizing data from multiple health systems in the Chicagoland region, can support work to advance diagnosis and management of IPV+BI.
n26b5d02099a0: The incidence distribution of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) and gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) cancers presents important geographic variations, yet the causes of these differences remain unclear. We analyzed 520 whole genomes from EAC/GEJ tumors across eight countries to examine the mutational forces shaping these cancers and their geographic variation. The mutational landscape was highly similar between EAC and GEJ tumors, and was dominated by signatures SBS17a/b, previously associated with reflux in EAC/GEJ. SBS17a/b were linked to obesity in EAC, supporting an indirect role in exacerbating reflux-mediated mutagenesis. Other established risk factors, such as tobacco smoking, did not yield a direct mutational footprint, pointing to non-mutagenic effects in EAC/GEJ. Nonetheless, geographic differences were present, with signatures related to endogenous cellular functions enriched in high-incidence populations. These findings provide new insights into the shared mutational forces that shape EAC and GEJ, as well as their geographic distribution.
na061fd10a583: Data on adolescent tobacco use in the Republic of Congo are scarce, despite a 2012 tobacco control law and 2018 decrees banning smoking in public places and tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship. This study aimed to estimate current tobacco product use among Congolese middle school students, identify associated factors, and develop a simple score to identify current use. Secondary analysis of the cross-sectional 2019 Global Youth Tobacco Survey (GYTS). Current use was defined as self-reported use, in the past 30 days, of cigarettes (CR7), other smoked tobacco products (CR10) or smokeless tobacco (CR14). The estimates and regression models accounted for the sampling weights, 34 strata and 70 primary sampling units. A point-based score was developed from eight questionnaire-based factors and evaluated via cross-validation, which was grouped by primary sampling unit. Among the 6,297 students with a usable tobacco use status, 842 reported current use; the weighted prevalence was 13.5% (95% CI: 11.1-16.3%). The full model included 5,251 students, 597 of whom were current users. Being offered free tobacco by a tobacco company representative (aOR = 3.05), exposure to smoke at home (aOR = 2.71), seeing teachers smoke at school (aOR = 2.60) and exposure to smoke in enclosed public places (aOR = 2.02) were associated with current use. The score, ranging from 0 to 18 points, had a weighted AUROC of 0.771 in the development data and 0.765 in the grouped cross-validation data. Current tobacco use affects a substantial proportion of middle-school students. The associations with social and commercial exposures support the strengthening of prevention and the enforcement of existing legislation. The score is exploratory and requires external validation before any operational use.
n201e4dd29241: Standardized outcome reporting is essential to generate timely and comparable evidence during epidemics. The World Health Organization (WHO) developed the Maternal and Neonatal Health during Epidemic Threats Core Outcome Set (MNH?EPI?COS) and a complementary Data Collection and Analysis Toolkit to support its implementation. Before global dissemination, the Toolkit required pilot testing to assess its usability, acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility across diverse research settings, identify challenges encountered by end users, and inform required improvements and refinements to the Toolkit. A four-phased mixed?methods evaluation was conducted with five research teams from Brazil, Honduras, India, Rwanda, and the United Kingdom. Teams received training and piloted all Toolkit components using retrospective datasets from previous epidemic contexts. Evaluation methods included structured feedback forms, observation of check?in meetings, and a virtual consultation. Findings informed an iterative process of refinement of the Toolkit components. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Twenty participants with expertise in epidemiology, clinical research, REDCap administration, and data and management analysis completed the pilot. The REDCap project, R scripts, and supporting materials (reference guide, virtual training session, and videos) were consistently rated as clear, well-structured, and feasible to use. Paper?based case report forms (CRFs) were comprehensive but required refinement, particularly regarding redundancy, and alignment with electronic forms. Teams emphasized the need for multilingual materials, specialized training in R, and strengthened data quality controls to enhance the quality of the evidence generated. The WHO MNH?EPI?COS Data Collection and Analysis Toolkit demonstrated strong usability, acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility across diverse settings. The findings informed targeted refinements and support the Toolkit's readiness for broader implementation to strengthen maternal and neonatal health research and surveillance during epidemics. Future evaluations should include prospective, real?time data collection during active outbreaks to further assess and strengthen the Toolkit's performance under operational epidemic conditions.
n1dc6dc07430a: Background: Resilience during the transition from middle childhood towards early adolescence is best understood as a dynamic, adversity-activated developmental process rather than a fixed individual trait. Building on the Resilient Kid in the Digital World framework, this protocol describes the longitudinal component of the broader research programme, designed to characterise developmental trajectories of resilience-related capacities and resources and adaptive functioning, identify their determinants, and examine prospective associations with risk experiences and behaviours across behavioural, family, school, and digital contexts. Methods: This is a national school-based cohort study following children aged 9-11 years at baseline across four waves at approximately six-month intervals from autumn 2025 to spring 2027. Schools are selected from the Czech national register using stratified probability-proportional-to-size sampling by region, municipality status, and area-level socioeconomic status; all eligible Grade 4 and Grade 5 pupils in participating schools are invited. The recruitment plan covers approximately 72 schools and 8,000 eligible children, with an anticipated 50-60% participation rate for complete child-parent pairs, corresponding to a target of approximately 4,000-4,800 linked child-parent dyads at baseline. Longitudinal planning aims to retain at least 1,000 linked dyads through Wave 4. Data are collected through child self-report, parent self- and proxy-report, and school-coordinator online questionnaires. Measures cover resilience-related capacities and resources, adaptive functioning and well-being, risk exposures, digital engagement, health-related behaviours, family context, parental mediation, and school context. Analyses will be tailored to the specific research questions and may include longitudinal and multilevel approaches complemented by reciprocal and person-oriented analyses. Discussion: The study provides a multi-dimensional, nationally distributed longitudinal resource for examining how child functioning and resilience-related resources change together with risk experiences and contextual conditions during a key developmental transition. The design explicitly distinguishes resilience-related measures from evidence of resilience under adversity and treats digital environments as one interacting developmental context rather than as an isolated exposure domain. The cohort may also inform understanding of early vulnerability and protective processes relevant to problematic digital engagement, without treating such indicators as clinical diagnoses.
nb16409e15b9a: Background: Emergency care requires appropriate triage and management as well as diagnosis. We compared five large language models on these tasks using the same clinical vignettes. Methods: Seventeen synthetic emergency department vignettes were submitted to Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5, Gemini 3.6 Flash and Kimi K3 through consumer interfaces on 11-12 August 2026. Two emergency physicians independently assessed the 85 responses with model identities concealed. Outcomes were agreement with reference diagnoses and Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) levels, appropriateness and overall quality (1-5 scales), potential harm and preferred response. Results: Every model correctly named the reference diagnosis in all 17 cases. CTAS exact agreement ranged from 14/17 to 15/17 per model (p=0.938). Of 13 discordant assignments, nine were undertriage and four overtriage. Appropriateness and quality differed across models (both p<0.001): Kimi K3 had the highest mean scores (4.82 and 4.74) and Grok 4.5 the lowest (3.91 and 3.71); Grok 4.5 scored significantly lower than every other model on both scales after Holm adjustment. Nine responses were flagged for potential harm: four from Grok 4.5, two each from Gemini 3.6 Flash and GPT-5.6 Sol, one from Claude Fable 5 and none from Kimi K3 (p=0.119). Conclusion: In this selected set of synthetic vignettes, all five models correctly named the reference diagnosis, yet undertriage and potentially harmful omissions occurred and response quality differed between models. These findings do not establish any model's clinical safety.
n78e1cb5fdc85: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by abnormal cortical activity, which can be captured using electroencephalography (EEG). Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for diagnosing several neurological conditions, comprehensive evaluation of classical ML and deep learning (DL) methods, together with physiologically meaningful explanations, remains limited for RTT. This study analyses resting-state, eyes-closed EEG recordings from RTT patients and healthy controls using both power spectral density (PSD)-based ML and end-to-end DL frameworks. Classical ML models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained on PSD features, while EEG-specific DL architectures, including ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer, were trained directly on preprocessed EEG signals. Subject-wise cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage, with balanced accuracy as the primary performance metric because it equally accounts for sensitivity and specificity. Random Forest achieved the best performance among the classical ML models, whereas EEGNet achieved the highest DL performance. An ablation study indicated that 4-second EEG epochs offered the optimal trade-off between model performance and robustness. Model interpretability was investigated using SHAP for Random Forest and occlusion sensitivity analysis for EEGNet. Both methods consistently identified delta and theta oscillations, along with centro-frontal brain regions, as key contributors to RTT classification. These findings show that both PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning methods can reliably identify RTT and highlight common neurophysiological biomarkers, offering an interpretable framework for EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker discovery for Rett Syndrome.
nf73b36abc53f: Importance. Hospital closures may alter access to emergency care. However, changes in utilization among residents of affected communities are less well characterized than changes in volume at surrounding hospitals. Objective. To compare changes in emergency department (ED) utilization among Madera County residents following the closure of Madera Community Hospital (MCH) with changes among Fresno County residents, and to examine geographic differences by pre-closure reliance on MCH. Design, Setting, and Participants. Retrospective population-based comparative study of annual California hospital Patient Origin/Market Share data, 2015-2024, with an exploratory comparative interrupted time-series analysis. Pre-pandemic years were 2015-2019, pandemic-affected pre-closure years were 2020-2022, and the two complete closure years were 2023-2024. Encounters were classified by county of patient residence, regardless of treating hospital location. Main Outcomes and Measures. Combined ED encounters (ED-only plus inpatient-from-ED) and each component separately. County-level utilization was expressed as encounters per 1,000 residents using annual population estimates. Geographic comparisons by pre-closure MCH dependence used ZIP-code encounter counts. Results. From 2022 to 2023, the first complete year following closure, combined ED utilization declined from 398.47 to 333.61 encounters per 1,000 Madera County residents (-16.3%), compared with 399.61 to 398.49 (-0.3%) among Fresno County residents. Madera ED-only rates declined 20.4%, while inpatient-from-ED rates increased 13.4%; however, the adjusted comparative analysis did not identify a consistent additional Madera-specific increase in inpatient-from-ED utilization. Exploratory regression estimated Madera-specific closure-period rate ratios of 0.871 for combined ED utilization and 0.848 for ED-only utilization. Combined ED encounter counts declined 18.4% in high-MCH-dependence ZIP codes versus 5.8% in low-dependence ZIP codes. Statistical inference was limited by the inclusion of only two counties, two complete closure years, and substantial overdispersion. Conclusions and Relevance. The period following MCH closure was associated with a substantial reduction in ED utilization among Madera County residents relative to Fresno County residents, concentrated in ED-only encounters and communities previously most dependent on MCH. The observational design does not establish causation or determine whether reduced utilization reflected substitution to other care settings, decreased demand, or unmet medical need.
n13f8498056bc: Background. Episignatures, disorder-specific patterns of genome-wide DNA methylation, are established for more than 100 Mendelian conditions and help resolve variants of uncertain significance and evaluate unsolved cases. Current clinical testing approaches typically use data generated by methylation arrays, which require a specific assay and limit discovery to the probe set of the array. Long-read and Illumina 5-base genome sequencing measure CpG methylation alongside genetic variation, raising the possibility of folding episignature analysis into a single genome-wide test. Methods. We sequenced individuals with SETD1B-related neurodevelopmental disorder, Kabuki syndrome, or Kleefstra syndrome, along with controls, using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), PacBio HiFi, or Illumina 5-base whole-genome sequencing. We identified differentially methylated regions (DMRs) directly from ONT methylation data and built classifiers using a nested cross-validation framework. Results. We identified 143 DMRs for SETD1B-related neurodevelopmental disorder (SETD1B-NDD), 20 for Kabuki syndrome, and 23 for Kleefstra syndrome; 15 to 26% of the DMRs across the three signatures contained no array probe(s). Cross-validated classifiers ranked every case above every control for all three conditions, and the final classifiers called all but one held-out case correctly, with the remaining case, which carries a KMT2D missense variant, as indeterminate. At two outside sites, the classifier for SETD1B-NDD correctly categorized seven out of seven cases. Principal component analysis reveals most PacBio and Illumina 5-base genomes cluster with ONT genomes from the same condition. One PacBio control fell between the other controls and the Kabuki cases, whereas the ONT and 5-base genomes for the same individual grouped with controls, suggesting platform-specific methylation differences that the current training cohort is too small to fully account for. Conclusions. Episignatures can be derived directly from sequencing data and applied across platforms. EpiSignaLR is an open workflow that combines the three ONT-derived classifiers with 34 published array-derived signatures. Developing robust sequencing-derived episignatures will require larger cohorts per condition and openly shared, platform-matched methylation data.
ne525ed13b358: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health challenge, particularly among displaced populations. These environments foster TB transmission due to overcrowding, poor living conditions, and inadequate healthcare access Objectives: To compare the proportion of tuberculosis (TB) cases detected through screening among displaced populations residing in internally displaced persons (IDP) and refugee settings with that among the general population in Benue State, Nigeria. Design: Quantitative observational study comparing TB screening and diagnostic findings across displaced and general populations. Setting: IDP camps, refugee settings and general-community screening locations in Benue State, Nigeria. Participants: A total of 1,938 individuals were screened: 1,143 in displaced settings and 795 in the general population. Participants were assessed for presumptive TB and underwent the applicable diagnostic evaluation. Primary and secondary outcome measures: The primary outcome was the proportion of screened individuals diagnosed with TB in displaced settings compared with the general population. Secondary outcomes were the numbers of presumptive TB cases and TB diagnoses classified as bacteriologically confirmed. Results: Among the 1,143 individuals screened in displaced settings, 128 presumptive TB cases were identified, with 46 confirmed cases (26 bacteriologically and 20 clinically). In contrast, only 3 TB cases (2 bacteriologically and 1 clinically) were detected among 795 individuals in the general population. The TB prevalence rate in displaced populations was 4.0%, significantly higher than the 0.4% observed in the general population. Conclusions: The study confirms a heightened TB burden in displaced communities, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.
ndc8338913873: Introduction: Preconception carrier screening (PCS) reduces monogenic disease incidence, exemplified by a 90% decline in Tay-Sachs among Ashkenazi populations. The Mexican Jewish Community (MJC), an endogamous population, may have increased prevalence of population-specific genetic disorders. The added value of exome sequencing (ES) over standard panels remains unclear. Objectives: To identify pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in autosomal recessive (AR), X-linked (XL), and mitochondrial genes, evaluate secondary findings (SF), and define population-specific allele frequencies in the MJC. Methods: From 2020-2025, 787 couples (1,574 individuals) underwent ES following counseling and consent. Genetic data was analyzed including SNVs, CNVs, and mitochondrial DNA. Reporting was limited to P/LP variants and SF. Results: Shared AR carrier status was identified in 49 couples (6.2%): 18.4% associated with severe, 16.3% moderate, and 65.3% with mild conditions. In 71.4% of couples, both partners carried the same variant, consistent with endogamy within the cohort. Maternal findings were identified in 10 women (1.27%). Clinically actionable SF were found in 2.85% of individuals. ES identified 12 at-risk couples (24.4%), undetected by standard panels. Individual genomic profiling revealed 920 rare P/LP variants, including 146 novel alleles, underscoring the distinct genetic architecture of the MJC. Conclusion: ES-based PCS improves detection of at-risk couples beyond conventional screening and supports its use in endogamous populations.
ndb388914638c: Objective: To determine whether combining four routine data sources improves in-hospital detection of lung cancer and heart failure, which sources drive each prediction, whether explanations are faithful, whether models are fair, and how much benefit federated training retains. Methods: In this retrospective single-centre study, we linked MIMIC-IV admissions (73,637 patients) to chest radiographs, radiology reports, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) and laboratory tests from the first 48 hours. For each disease, excluding prior cases, we compared single-source models, gradient boosting and early, late and attention-based fusion on patient-level splits. We tested explanations for faithfulness and weight dependence, audited performance by sex, age, race and ethnicity, and insurance, and simulated five unequal hospitals to compare federated, centralised and local training. Results: Lung cancer was coded in 1.7% and heart failure in 15.6% of patients. For lung cancer, attention fusion reached an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.833 (95% CI 0.809-0.859) against 0.753 for gradient boosting on laboratory data; for heart failure, 0.885 (0.878-0.892) against 0.794 (both p < 0.001). Early and late fusion performed similarly. Laboratory data and radiology reports contributed most to lung cancer, and the ECG to heart failure. Explanations passed a deletion test; a weight-randomisation check on absolute attributions passed for ECG but not for laboratory explanations. For heart failure, discrimination fell with age. Federated training recovered 95% of the centralised gain over local training for heart failure; for lung cancer, federated averaging (FedAvg) recovered 51% and FedProx 82%. Conclusion: Fusing routine data improved in-hospital detection of both diseases over laboratory data alone, and which data matter depends on the disease. Explanation checks should be run per source and per similarity measure, and performance in older patients monitored. For the rare outcome, FedProx, which limits drift between sites, retained more of the pooled benefit than FedAvg. External validation is needed.
nd18a5f5eb202: Background: Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown. Methods: We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients. Results: ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001). Discussion: These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.
n00e24d5ae58d: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) might reduce tobacco and alcohol use. We synthesised evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on smoking and alcohol outcomes, including secondary outcomes reported in trials conducted for other clinical purposes. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, CENTRAL, PubMed, and registries for RCTs comparing GLP-1RAs with placebo from inception to August 18, 2026. Smoking and alcohol outcomes were synthesised using random-effects meta-analyses. We assessed risk of bias (RoB) with RoB-2, and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Findings Fourteen trials involving 1149 participants were included; 13 contributed to meta-analyses. Across the 14 trials, 8 recruited participants not seeking either tobacco or alcohol treatment. The other 6 recruited treatment-seeking participants: 3 for tobacco and 3 for alcohol. Eight trials reported smoking-related outcomes, 11 reported alcohol outcomes, and 5 reported both. Follow-up ranged from 6 to 60 weeks. All 4 pooled smoking-related estimates favoured GLP-1RAs, although all 95% CIs included no difference and were compatible with increases and decreases in outcomes; e.g., smoking cessation, OR 1.39 (95% CI, 0.77 to 2.53, k=3). Restricting analyses to semaglutide trials indicated a reduction in cigarettes per day (CPD) (SMD=-0.10, 95%CI:-0.16 to -0.04; k=3). Across agents, pooled estimates favoured GLP-1RAs for days without alcohol (SMD=0.35, 95%CI: 0.12 to 0.59, k=3). Pooled estimates of semaglutide-only trials also favoured treatment for alcohol consumption (grams/day; SMD=-0.56, 95%CI:-0.82 to -0.30; k=2), craving (SMD=-0.60, 95%CI:-0.91 to -0.29; k=2), drinks per drinking day (SMD=-0.59, 95%CI:-0.86 to -0.32; k=3), drinks per calendar day (SMD=-0.48, 95%CI:-0.87 to -0.09; k=2) and heavy drinking days (SMD=-0.45, 95%CI:-0.85 to -0.06; k=3), and alcohol-free days (SMD=0.41, 95%CI:0.09 to 0.73; k=2). Two of 41 assessed results were at low RoB, 31 raised some concerns and 8 were at high risk; certainty was moderate for 1 outcome, low for 4 and very low for 8. Interpretation GLP-1RAs may reduce alcohol consumption and CPD, with the clearest evidence for semaglutide. These findings should be contextualised by most evidence being low- to very-low-certainty. Larger trials are needed to establish clinically meaningful benefit and sustained abstinence.
nc626f422c35a: Lyme disease is a vector-borne bacterial infection with marked heterogeneity in susceptibility and clinical manifestations. We investigated the genetic architecture and clinical heterogeneity of Lyme disease using genetic and longitudinal health data from FinnGen and the Estonian Biobank. Genome-wide association analyses included 37,571 individuals with Lyme disease and 670,567 controls (N = 708,138), complemented by sex-stratified analyses and temporal phenotyping in FinnGen. The overall GWAS meta-analysis identified three genome-wide significant loci at SCGB1D2, TLR1/TLR6, and HLA-DQA1. Sex-stratified analyses identified additional genome-wide significant signals at CPE in males (beta = -0.077, P = 2.99e-8) and the TYMP-CPT1B locus in females (beta = -0.064, P = 4.98e-8). The TLR1/6 association was more pronounced in males (beta = -0.141, P = 2.16e-12) than in females (beta = -0.060, P = 1.21e-5). Temporal phenotyping showed enrichment of neurological, musculoskeletal, and dermatological manifestations after Lyme disease diagnosis, with associations generally attenuating over time. Bell palsy showed the strongest association at 1-6 months (OR 11.49, P = 2.37e-79), while joint pain was also enriched during this interval (OR 1.74, P = 1.95e-23). Early associations with joint pain and Bell palsy were stronger in males than in females. These findings expand the genetic architecture of Lyme disease, implicate innate immune sensing through the TLR1/TLR6 locus, and antigen presentation through the HLA associations. Overall, the results highlight a strong polygenic signal with Lyme disease and a connection with other post-infectious clinical manifestations.
n5644c5ed0094: Background: Cortical N1 responses to balance perturbations are larger and earlier with increasing magnitude and differ with reactive stepping. Whether stroke alters this modulation is unknown. Objective: To compare N1 modulation across perturbation magnitudes and reactive balance outcomes in older adults with and without stroke. We hypothesized that people with stroke would show greater N1 scaling than controls; that larger N1s at small perturbations would limit scaling (a recruitment ceiling); and that stroke would constrain N1 modulation by stepping outcome. Methods: Sixteen people with chronic stroke (66+/-11 years) and 15 age-similar controls (68+/-8 years) received forward support-surface perturbations at a small standardized magnitude and at individual step thresholds (~50% unintentional steps). N1 peak amplitude and latency were compared across magnitudes in feet-in-place trials, and between stepping and feet-in-place trials at step threshold. N1 scaling was the relative amplitude increase between magnitudes. Results: Despite lower clinical balance after stroke (p<0.001), step thresholds were similar between groups. N1s were larger with shorter latencies at step threshold in both groups (p<0.001), but scaled more after stroke (44% vs 13%,p=0.009). Greater scaling was associated with smaller small-magnitude N1s after stroke (B=0.43, p=0.041) and higher step thresholds across groups (B=0.35, p=0.048). N1 latency was 11 ms longer in stepping trials in controls but not after stroke (interaction p=0.024). Conclusions: Scaling of cortical recruitment with increasing perturbation magnitude may support reactive balance, and may be an adaptive mechanism for people after stroke. Less flexible N1 timing after stroke may limit cortical tuning to balance recovery strategy.
n6d0675f75ff8: Background: Evidence on menopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and disability progression in women with multiple sclerosis (MS) is limited, particularly in the era of high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy. We estimated the association between systemic HRT and sustained disability progression and recurring relapses in a contemporary national cohort. Methods: In a nationwide Swedish registry-based cohort, we followed women with MS aged 40 to 60 years entering from 2006 through 2024, with follow-up through 2025, under a new-user design. Systemic HRT was modeled as time-varying current use and quarterly oral-equivalent dose categories. Outcomes were sustained Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) 4.0, sustained EDSS 6.0, and recurring relapses. Cox models adjusted for baseline covariates and time-varying age and disease-modifying therapy (DMT) class. Results: Among 7,623 women, 1,192 (15.6%) initiated HRT. Current HRT use was associated with a lower hazard of sustained EDSS 4.0 (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51 to 0.96) but not sustained EDSS 6.0 (aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.16) or recurring relapses (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.36). Dose categories showed no consistent gradient. Raising the cohort-entry age floor to 50 years gave a consistent EDSS 4.0 estimate (aHR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.95). Conclusions: HRT was not associated with increased relapse risk or severe disability progression. The lower hazard of sustained EDSS 4.0 was not mirrored at EDSS 6.0 and showed no dose gradient. Given menopausal status was unmeasured, replication in cohorts with verified menopausal status is required for clear clinical interpretation.
n467fc296b9b7: Aims: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome highlights the interrelationship between metabolic, renal, and cardiovascular disorders. However, whether CKM burden influences longitudinal cardiac structural and functional recovery and subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear. Methods: We studied 1,600 patients from the STRATS-HHD registry who underwent echocardiography at baseline and 6-18 months after treatment initiation. CKM burden was defined by obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and severe hypertension (0-1, 2, or [≥]3 components). The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (HHF). Results: CKM burden was 0-1 in 973 patients (60.8%), 2 in 440 (27.5%), and [≥]3 in 187 (11.7%). Higher burden was associated with worse baseline cardiac abnormalities and increased primary outcome risk (adjusted HR, 3.09; 95% CI, 1.92-4.98 for [≥]3 vs 0-1; adjusted HR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.27-1.84 per +1 CKM component). The prognostic association persisted after additional adjustment for hepatic steatosis index-defined metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Despite overall improvement in most echocardiographic parameters after treatment, patients with CKM burden [≥]3 showed less favorable E/e', LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), and LA stiffness index at follow-up. Normalization of these parameters at follow-up was associated with substantially lower subsequent cardiovascular risk. Mediation analyses suggested that echocardiographic abnormalities partially mediated the association between high CKM burden and the primary outcome. Conclusion: CKM burden identifies hypertensive patients with less favorable cardiac function after treatment and increased cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight the association of CKM burden with cardiac functional recovery and prognosis in patients with hypertension.
nb65a3a695b2e: Insomnia, depression and anxiety co-occur and share genetic liability, but a genetic correlation cannot show whether that liability is spread across the sleep domain or concentrated in insomnia, a diagnostic criterion for depression and generalized anxiety disorder. We applied genomic structural equation modelling to ten genome-wide association studies and fitted a four-factor model of sleep, internalizing (depression and anxiety), psychotic-bipolar and metabolic liability. A model linking the sleep and internalizing domains only through their factor correlation was inadmissible, and we compared, under one decision rule, each one-parameter link that could repair it: domain-wide links, an insomnia-specific cross-loading, and residual covariances representing shared diagnostic content, of which three were admissible. The insomnia cross-loading fitted better than the only admissible domain-wide alternative ({Delta}AIC = 13.8; better in 98.6% of 500 Monte Carlo draws) and than shared content ({Delta}AIC = 96.9), and placing it on psychotic-bipolar or metabolic liability was inadmissible. Under this model the insomnia pathway carried 56.3% of the sleep-internalizing covariance (95% CI 45.6-67.0%). A second sleep pathway improved fit ({Delta}AIC = -33.3), but with three sleep indicators its location was not identifiable, and across the equivalent models the insomnia share ranged from 0% to 127.0%. At the variant level, no internalizing lead departed from depression-anxiety proportionality after correction, and internalizing leads replicated in FinnGen, with partial sample overlap, whereas sleep leads did not (60.4%; P = 0.17). How concentrated the overlap is will require finer sleep phenotypes to establish. Among single-link models, insomnia is the best-supported location of the overlap.
n330f94f491a3: Background: Women with multiple sclerosis (MS) have fewer children than other women, but whether this narrowed as pregnancy evidence became reassuring and treatment options expanded is uncertain. Objective: To compare live birth trends from 2004 to 2022 between women with MS and all Swedish women. Methods: Linking the Swedish MS, National Patient, and Medical Birth Registers with national statistics, we compared age-standardised live birth rates, counted expected births at national rates, and estimated adjusted annual live-birth risk ratios in a matched comparison sample. Results: Women with MS (n=10,452; 76,989 woman-years) had 3,577 children, about 1,200 (25%) fewer than expected (observed-to-expected ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.72 to 0.77). Standardised rate ratios were below 1 annually (median 0.77). Observed-to-expected ratios were 0.73 (0.68 to 0.79) in 2004 to 2008 and 0.70 (0.65 to 0.75) in 2019 to 2022 (population-by-period interaction p=0.31). Age- and region-adjusted risk ratios ranged from 0.75 to 0.86 across periods (heterogeneity p=0.020), closest to 1 in 2009 to 2013. Conclusion: Women with MS had about one quarter fewer live births than other Swedish women, and the difference was similar in the first and last periods.
nb3b140fcfba4: Community health workers (CHWs) are central to primary healthcare delivery in low-resource settings, yet evidence on what sustains their engagement beyond a decade is limited, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined long-term retention and its associated factors among volunteer CHWs in southwestern Uganda, 17 to 21 years after their initial selection and training. We conducted a quantitative retrospective cohort study using a census approach in April 2024 across three districts in south western Uganda where a cohort of CHWs were selected and trained between 2004 and 2008. Data were collected in April 2024 using a pretested, structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire. Data were analysed using STATA version 14.1. Descriptive statistics characterized the study population, stratified by retention status. Bivariate and Multivariable Poisson regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with long term retention of CHWs. From the 404 CHWs selected and trained in the period 2004-2008, 265 (65.6%) were still resident in the study districts. Of 265 CHWs, 161 (60.8%) were categorized as retained. Factors independently associated with retention were: peer support (adjusted incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.48-3.32, p < 0.001), always having access to reporting tools (adjusted IRR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.10-1.95, p = 0.01), and intermittent access to reporting tools (adjusted IRR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.08-1.79, p = 0.01). The most common reasons for exit were family duties, poor personal health, and community rejection. Over 60% of trained CHWs remained active after nearly two decades, indicating that volunteer CHW programmes can achieve sustained long-term engagement. Peer support and reliable access to reporting tools were the strongest modifiable predictors of retention. Strengthening these low-cost programmatic supports may be a cost-effective strategy for improving CHW retention in similar low-resource settings, and programme managers should prioritise structured peer-support networks and a consistent supply of reporting tools.
ncebd6ebd4ce6: Background: Glaucoma remains one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is an important modifiable risk factor for disease progression. Monitoring changes in IOP over time is therefore essential for glaucoma management. However, evidence on the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and its associated factors remains limited in resource-limited settings. This study investigated the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and its associated demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical determinants among glaucoma patients at Jimma University Medical Center. Objective: To assess the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and identify demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors associated with changes in IOP among glaucoma patients at Jimma University Medical Center. Method: A retrospective longitudinal study was conducted among glaucoma patients who had at least three follow-up visits at Jimma University Medical Center. Repeated IOP measurements were obtained over six follow-up waves from January 2022 to January 2024. Profile plots were used to describe the longitudinal pattern of IOP, and linear mixed-effects models were fitted to assess factors associated with baseline IOP and changes in IOP over time. Separate models were fitted for the left and right eyes, in addition to a bivariate model that jointly accounted for both eyes. Results: IOP generally declined over follow-up period, although the magnitude and rate of decline varied across patient characteristics and treatment groups. In the right Eye, rural residence was associated with lower baseline IOP, while occupation and treatment regimen was also significantly associated with baseline IOP. Significant time-by-occupation and time-by-treatment interactions were observed. In particular, right-eye IOP declined more rapidly among patients receiving Timolol with Diamox and Timolol with Xolamol. In the left eye, sex, occupation, treatment regimen, and treatment duration were associated with baseline IOP, while significant interactions between time and Timolol with Latanoprost and short treatment duration were observed. A bivariate model similarly showed significant effects of residence, occupation, and treatment regimen, as well as significant time-by-treatment interactions, indicating different longitudinal IOP trajectories across treatment groups. Conclusion: IOP trajectories differed between the two eyes, with a significant decline in left-eye IOP but no significant overall temporal change in right-eye IOP. Treatment regimen was the most consistent factor associated with differences in the longitudinal trajectory of IOP, while occupation, residence, and treatment duration also showed significant associations in selected analyses. These findings highlight the importance of longitudinal monitoring and consideration of patient and treatment characteristics when assessing IOP among glaucoma patients. Further longitudinal studies with larger and more diverse populations are warranted to investigate additional behavioral, environmental, and clinical factors influencing IOP trajectories.
n4402ab878308: Background: Accurate amyloid subtyping is essential for patient management but remains challenging with antibody-based methods. We prospectively evaluated a standardized LC-MS/MS workflow for routine amyloid typing, focusing on diagnostic yield, operational performance, and added value in cases not fully resolved by conventional methods. Methods: From 2020 to 2025, 115 FFPE biopsies from patients with suspected amyloidosis were analyzed at Hospital Universitario A Coruna, Spain, without laser microdissection. Proteins were identified and quantified using PEAKS, with a peak-area cutoff [≥]10 for candidate fibril proteins. Results: Seventy-nine cases (69%) were amyloid-positive, 22 (19%) negative and 14 (12%) indeterminate. AL (51%), ATTR (32%) and AA (10%) predominated, with additional AH (5%), mixed ATTR+AL, hereditary ATTRv and AIns amyloidoses. Binary concordance with conventional techniques ranged from 85.7% to 91.5%. LC-MS/MS provided additional diagnostic information in 64/110 evaluable cases (58.2%), including additional subtyping information in 53/110 (48.2%). The workflow also enabled relative quantification of variant versus wild-type TTR peptides and characterization of SAA post-translational modifications. Mean turnaround time was approximately two weeks and MS findings informed clinical management. Conclusions: LC-MS/MS amyloid typing was clinically feasible in routine FFPE biopsies without laser microdissection and supported identification of common, rare and mixed amyloid types.
n5c7725341078: Cuff-based blood pressure (BP) measurement is a cornerstone of health assessment, yet its mechanism remains unclear and measurement error remains substantial1. On the basis of membrane theory2,3, we propose that external pressure generated by cuff inflation follows a hyperbolic-cosine-shaped axial distribution along the artery, forming a pressure-peak zone (PPZ) beneath the cuff. By combining this external pressure with intra-arterial pressure, we constructed a mathematical model that systematically predicts site-specific vascular motion and hemodynamic changes during BP measurement. In humans, multimodal experiments integrating vascular imaging and synchronized invasive and noninvasive pressure measurements validated the model. The PPZ organizes distinct proximal and distal hemodynamics during cuff pressurization: at DBP, diastolic arterial collapse begins at the PPZ; near SBP, only weak residual blood flow traverses the PPZ and disappears once cuff pressure exceeds SBP. These transitions generated identifiable oscillogram features for DBP and SBP, precisely localized by wavelet scanning. The resulting method showed higher accuracy and lower variability than auscultation and conventional oscillometry and was the only method whose estimates did not differ significantly from invasive BP. This study redefines the hemodynamic basis of cuff-based BP measurement, and its mechanistic framework and accuracy may support clinical application and more reliable therapeutic decision-making.
n4e845367e572: Background Raw milk consumption has repeatedly been shown to be inversely related to asthma, respiratory infections, and allergies but carries a potential risk of life-threatening infections. The MARTHA trial (DRKS00014781) used minimally-processed pasteurized milk as a microbiologically safe proxy for raw milk and compared it against ultra-heat-treated milk for efficacy on atopic sensitization, asthma, and respiratory infections. Methods Healthy children were recruited through birth clinics in Germany. At 6 to 12 months, they were centrally randomized to obtain minimally-processed full-cream versus ultra-heat-treated semi-skimmed cow's milk daily until age 3 years. During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, recruitment was stopped, and the study was continued without confirmatory intention. The primary endpoint was shifted from asthma as composite parent-reported diagnosis of asthma or recurrent obstructive bronchitis until age 5 to atopic sensitization at age 3 years. Participants, caregivers, and study staff were blinded to group assignments. Results We randomized 130 individuals into each study arm. The intervention was unrelated to atopic sensitization (risk ratio, RR=1.13 [0.67-1.89]), which occurred in 28 individuals of the intervention (n=99) and 24 of the comparator group (n=96). Asthma showed a trend for an inverse association (hazards ratio, HR=0.55 [0.27;1.16], n=252), which was pronounced in the 82 children with a family history of asthma (post-hoc HR=0.30 [0.09;0.93]). The intervention was inversely associated with rhinitis and cough in the older half of the children (post-hoc RR=0.82 [0.67-0.998] and RR=0.75 [0.60-0.94], respectively). No adverse events were judged intervention-related. Interpretation The intervention did not reduce atopic sensitization at age 3 years. Exploratory analyses suggested possible protective effects on asthma and respiratory symptoms, particularly in children with parental asthma and in those less affected by pandemic-related disruptions. These findings justify but do not replace a definitive trial. Funding Dutch Longfonds; Bavarian State-Ministry of Health, Care and Prevention; German Center for Lung Research (DZL); FrieslandCampina.
n03b0f5a45fff: Background: The Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) measures information processing speed, and repeated testing can increase scores through practice effects. However, how differences in testing frequency bear on comparisons between disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in real-world cohorts has not been fully explored. Objective: To compare SDMT trajectories between natalizumab and rituximab users and quantify the association of the testing process with those trajectories. Methods: Using the Swedish MS Registry, we studied adults with relapsing-remitting MS initiating natalizumab or rituximab (2010-2024) with >=2 on-treatment SDMT assessments. Mixed-effects models with restricted cubic spline time were sequentially adjusted; log cumulative test number was the practice-effect adjustment. Results: Among 2,458 individuals, natalizumab initiators were tested twice as often as rituximab initiators (1.6 vs. 0.8 tests/year). The predicted natalizumab-minus-rituximab SDMT difference at 3 years was 7.0 points (95% CI 5.7-8.3) unadjusted and 1.6 (0.7-2.6) after full adjustment including cumulative test number; at 1 year it fell from 4.4 (3.3-5.4) to -0.3 (-1.2 to 0.6). Conclusion: Adjustment for cumulative test number substantially attenuated the SDMT difference between natalizumab and rituximab, leaving a small residual difference of uncertain clinical importance and underscoring the need to account for testing frequency in real-world comparisons.
ne21a49881013: Approximately half of all pancreatic cancers cannot be explained by known risk factors. Here we present the results of mutational signature analysis in 495 cases of pancreatic cancer from nine countries to explore whether there are previously unknown mutagenic exposures acting on pancreatic cancer genomes. The mutational signature landscape was consistent between countries. We identified one signature not previously found in pancreatic cancer, SBS111, which does not have a confirmed aetiology but is present in >99% of cases and contributes on average 26% of the total mutation burden. No evidence was found for mutational signatures known to be caused by exogenous exposures, nor was any mutational signature capable of explaining differences in incidence rates between countries. These results suggest that the unexplained causes of pancreatic cancer are unlikely to be strongly mutagenic and that non-mutagenic mechanisms may have a prominent role in explaining pancreatic cancer incidence.
nd43f53607712: Objectives To evaluate the impact of Score MAMA, Ecuador's national obstetric early-warning system, on rates of severe obstetric complications (hypertensive, hemorrhagic, septic), comparing the 2015 pilot phase (Zones 4/9) with the 2016 national rollout. Methods Quasi-experimental ecological interrupted time series study using national administrative data from Ecuador (2012-2024). The denominator came from the live-birth registry (ENV-INEC; n = 3 581 602); the numerator came from hospital discharge records (EDG-INEC), classified by ICD-10 code as Blue Code (O14-O15), Red Code (O44-O46/O67/O72), or Yellow Code (O85-O86/O41.1), aggregated monthly across Ecuador's 9 SENPLADES zones. Negative binomial models with a live-birth offset and zone-nested first-order autoregressive (AR1) correlation estimated incidence rate ratios (IRR). A secondary national-annual analysis modeled maternal mortality by code. Results We identified 200 075 discharges for an obstetric complication (Blue = 125 848; Red = 55 049; Yellow = 19 178). Blue Code increased in the pilot phase (IRR 1.27; 95% CI 1.03-1.57) and nationally (IRR 1.20; 95% CI 1.09-1.33); Red and Yellow Code showed no change. A national mortality analysis (817 deaths) found no significant change for any code (IRR 0.76-1.62; CI spanned 1). Conclusions Score MAMA was associated with a selective increase in recorded hypertensive complications, with no change in hemorrhage, sepsis, or maternal mortality -- a pattern more consistent with improved detection of preeclampsia-eclampsia than a true change in complication incidence.
n924b6dab0c60: Background: The stabilisation of infants at birth is vital for survival and relies on clinicians being appropriately trained in neonatal resuscitation. The effectiveness of resuscitation is influenced by the skills, knowledge and equipment available to the responding clinician. In Australia, the absence of a standardised neonatal resuscitation training programme may contribute to variations in training practices. This study aimed to describe current training practices across Australian public services and explore educators perceptions of opportunities for national standardisation. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was distributed to educators and representatives from birth and newborn care public facilities across Australia. A questionnaire was developed to gain knowledge on how newborn resuscitation is taught detailing staffing, equipment and training requirements. Results: 197 completed responses were received. Responses were received from all Australian states and territories and levels of maternity/neonatal services. Accreditation in neonatal resuscitation was required by 173 (87.8%) of respondents programmes with training occurring at annual (n=95, 47.7%) or more frequent (n=21, 10.7%) intervals. NeoResus (n=134, 67.5%), Neonatal Advanced Life Support (n=45, 22.8%) and Newborn Life Support Training (n=41, 21.3%) were the most popular training programmes. Substantial variation was identified in equipment used for training. Most respondents (n=174, 88.3%) reported a need for a standardised national training programme. Conclusions: Neonatal resuscitation training is widely available in Australian public facilities, but reported requirements, programmes, content, assessment methods and training resources vary. These findings support the development of standardised neonatal resuscitation training to promote consistent preparedness across Australian healthcare settings.
n272f2edde035: Objective: To examine trends in use of nicotine pouches as a smoking cessation aid, characteristics of people using pouches during smoking quit attempts, the characteristics of quit attempts involving pouches, and the real-world association between pouch use and quit success. Design: Monthly cross-sectional survey. Setting: Great Britain. Participants: 7,995 adults ([≥]18 years) who reported making a serious attempt to stop smoking in the past year, surveyed between June 2021 and July 2026. Main outcome measures: Participants reported use of nicotine pouches during the most recent smoking quit attempt (yes/no). Quit success was defined as reporting that the participant was still not smoking following the attempt. Associations between pouch use and quit success were estimated using logistic regression, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, use of other cessation aids, characteristics of the quit attempt, strength of urges to smoke, and survey year. Results: Among adults who attempted to quit smoking, the proportion using pouches as a cessation aid increased from 2.4% [95%CI 1.3-4.1%] in June 2021 to 6.7% [4.6-9.6%] in July 2026 (prevalence ratio [PR]=2.83 [1.37-5.81]), with particularly large increases among 18-24-year-olds (2.2% to 18.9%; PR=8.75 [4.15-26.79]) and men (1.8% to 11.0%; PR=6.05 [3.19-14.31]). In 2024-26, 43.8% of those using pouches as a cessation aid were aged 18-24 and 69.5% were men. Pouch users also commonly reported using e-cigarettes (49.6%) or over-the-counter nicotine replacement therapy (37.9%) during the same quit attempt. Unadjusted quit success was 33.5% [27.1-39.9] among pouch users compared with 27.0% [25.9-28.1] among those who did not use pouches (OR=1.36 [1.02-1.82]). After adjustment, the association was attenuated (ORadj=1.15 [0.80-1.65]), with the 95%CI compatible with both a modest adverse association and a modest to large benefit. The association differed according to concurrent e-cigarette use (pinteraction=0.002): among those not using e-cigarettes as a cessation aid, pouch use was associated with higher quit success (ORadj=1.91 [1.23-2.97]), whereas evidence of an association among e-cigarette users was uncertain (ORadj=0.63 [0.36-1.11]). Conclusions: Use of nicotine pouches as a smoking cessation aid increased substantially in Great Britain between 2021 and 2026, particularly among younger adults and men. Pouches were frequently used alongside other cessation aids. While the overall association with quit success was uncertain, pouch use was associated with higher quit success among those not using e-cigarettes. If causal, this suggests a potential role for pouches among people not already using an established cessation aid.
n302af4365a69: Objective: Clinical pharmacists improve medication management and safety in intensive care units, yet their role in neonatal and pediatric intensive care remains highly variable across institutions. Evidence supporting standardized clinical pharmacy practice models in these settings is limited. This study evaluated the association between pharmacist service coverage and clinical outcomes in critically ill pediatric patients. Design: Multicenter, observational study with prospective and retrospective data collection. Setting: ICUs at participating institutions in the United States and internationally. Patients: Patients <18 years of age Intervention: None Measurements: The primary exposure was pharmacist-led comprehensive medication management (CMM) with daily participation in multidisciplinary rounds. The secondary exposure was the pharmacist-to-ICU-patient ratio. The primary outcome was hazard of discharge alive (HDA) from the ICU. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, hospital HDA, and hazard of extubation alive (HEA). Fine-Gray competing risks models and multivariable Firth logistic regression were used for adjusted analyses. Main results: A total of 1,459 patients cared for by 69 clinical pharmacists across 31 institutions were included. Daily CMM with rounding was associated with a higher HDA from the ICU (HR 2.60, 95% CI 2.17-3.10; p<0.001), higher HDA from the hospital (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.83-2.75; p<0.001), and a higher HEA (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10-1.33; p<0.001), but not with in-hospital mortality (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.14-1.36; p=0.154). The pharmacist-to-ICU-patient ratio was not significantly associated with ICU HDA (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.01; p=0.88) or any secondary outcome. Conclusions: Daily pharmacist-provided CMM with multidisciplinary ICU rounding was associated with improved discharge outcomes among critically ill pediatric and neonatal patients, whereas pharmacist-to-ICU-patient ratio alone was not. These findings support standardized integration of clinical pharmacists into daily multidisciplinary rounds in this setting.
n5e8eaebf0ebf: Data from medical records are often limited in size, creating challenges for Artificial Intelligence training, and an opportunity for data augmentation techniques to create synthetic data. A natural question is how much data can be randomized and still be realistic. The main goal of this study is to attempt to measure the reproducibility of labs drawn in practice, so these ranges can be used for generating more realistic synthetic data. A second goal is to inform clinicians of the real error ranges of their laboratory data so these values may be better interpreted.
